features.text: The patient is a 44-year-old female.
The patient has had hematuria for about six weeks.
The hematuria is bright red, like cherry Kool-Aid.
The hematuria is intermittent.
The patient experienced pain in the lower back area with a severity of 8 out of 10.
The pain was constant and severe but has improved after passing the stones.
The patient has not had fever, nausea, or vomiting.
The patient has a 6 mm stone in the left kidney, not blocking anything.
The right kidney measures 10 cm long and 5 cm wide.
The left kidney measures 10.8 cm long.
The ultrasound showed no stones, masses, or hydronephrosis in the right kidney.
The patient had a trace amount of blood in the urine, but nothing else was abnormal.
The patient has had frequent urination and urgency, especially before passing the stones.
The patient has not experienced dysuria or a history of urinary tract infections.
The patient has not experienced fever, chills, or flank tenderness.
The patient has not experienced changes in urinary stream, such as difficulty starting urination, weak flow, or intermittent flow.
The patient is unsure about family history of kidney stones or related conditions.
The patient drinks more Mountain Dew than water and consumes a lot of processed foods and meat.
The patient does not eat much fruits or vegetables.
The patient has not had a CT urography or other imaging studies besides the renal ultrasound.
The patient has not had any swelling in the legs or abdomen.
The patient's urine is mostly clear and yellow, with no changes in color or frequency other than what was already mentioned.
